option_evidence: its own line and the line beneath it

sections.heading: For every narrower kind you list under a record, this must hold:

rules.text: A record is listed under a narrower kind only when the record's own words, about its subject, supply the feature that tells that kind from its siblings; quote that feature. Where the kinds differ only in a property the record never mentions, the record names none of them, and {{parent_entity}} is the answer.

sections.heading: Match each narrower kind you identified by the first of these rules that applies, in order:

rules.text: An option is an exact match when what it means — {{option_evidence}} — is the narrower kind you identified. Compare meanings, never names: an option whose name resembles what you identified is not chosen when what it means does not cover it.

When no option is an exact match, an option is a generalizing match when what it means includes the narrower kind you identified while remaining narrower than {{parent_entity}}, and the list holds nothing narrower that the record supports. A generalizing match never stands alone: the narrower kind it generalizes is proposed beside it under its own name.

When no option exactly matches the narrower kind you identified — whether or not one generalizes it — propose it under a plain, generic name, a sibling of the options listed: the name the list would carry for it, as short as the list's own entries, naming the kind itself and not the relationship to it. One proposal names one kind; a name that lists or joins several is not a name. A proposal that restates an option under other words is that option, and is matched instead.
